text:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up on the onboarding gates pipeline. TL;DR: add perf + compatibility + semantic checks, make gates pluggable, and emit machine-readable artifacts for rollouts. Thoughts?

maria: Like the direction. Need to nail which perf metrics we gate on: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, peak GPU memory? Also how do we weigh cost vs perf for hosted vs dedicated?

devon: I vote for two perf profiles: interactive (latency SLO) and batch (throughput SLO). Each profile should have a synthetic trace generator to mimic typical request shapes.

chris: +1. Also we must validate tokenizer/vocab compatibility early. A model with a different tokenizer hash will silently break prompt parsing for customers. We should gate on tokenizer hash and tokenizer API surface.

kate: We should fail fast on config/schema incompatibilities and include migration hints. Propose a field in the registry: "compatibility_status" with reasons if failed.

infra-bot: automated test run started: model-id=redwood/xyz run=perf+compat check-run-id=1740001400

alex: Example of the gating config I'm imagining: 
```yaml
checks:
  - name: perf
    type: latency
    thresholds:
      p50: 50ms
      p95: 200ms
  - name: compat
    type: tokenizer
    required_hash: "abc123"
  - name: semantics
    type: eval
    dataset: sanity_promptset
    pass_rate: 0.9
```

maria: Semantics evals need an explicit seed + versioned promptset. Also we need to pin the evaluation harness container image so results are reproducible.

devon: Important: quantization-aware checks. We need to run the int8 path (or other quantized runtime) during onboarding and compare semantic scores within a small delta — can't just gate on FP32 runs.

chris: Edge-case for Private deployments: customers may build custom kernels. We should include a binary-compat check (kernel-version / build-id) so we don't silently pass something that will fail on-prem.

kate: Rollout flow idea: gate -> canary (10%) -> ramp. The gate must produce a signed JSON artifact with checks, scores, and provenance (git commit, image digest). Rollout service will consume that artifact.

deploy-bot: deploy-plan created: model=redwood/xyz, canary=10%, fallback=redwood/xyz:fp16, plan_id=pl-1740002000

alex: Ownership question: who maintains promptsets and gold labels? Suggest shared ownership between Research and SRE/Platform. Also where do we store artifacts? I'd like a canonical path: s3://redwood-models/onboard/1740001234/

maria: @devon can you sketch the minimal plugin API for a gate? Something like `run_checks(model_uri, runtime_descriptor, opts) -> {status, results_url}` so different teams can add gates.

devon: Yep. Minimal contract: accept model manifest URL, target runtime descriptor (cpu/gpu/quant), and options. Return pass/fail + artifact links + per-check metadata. I'll draft an interface PR and include example adapters for tokenizer/perf/semantic checks.

ops-bot: Note: perf CI quota is limited during business hours; current queue ETA for full perf suite ~2h.

alex: Great. Next steps: devon will PR the plugin interface, kate will draft the rollout artifact schema, maria will enumerate required promptsets and seeds, and I'll update the RFC with these action items and timelines. Thanks all :thumbsup:
